articles.summary: An agent with a good model and no company context writes copy any competitor could have sent. The four things context actually means (knowledge, state, tools, memory), how to give an agent each one as code, and how to keep them true once they are deployed.
articles.title: Building and Contextualizing Autonomous GTM Agents

articles.summary: A software factory treats go-to-market as a development process: revenue logic built, versioned and deployed as code, operated by agents that read your company's knowledge at runtime. What the model requires, and why context is the constraint rather than the model.
articles.title: Building a Software Factory for Go-to-Market

articles.summary: A clean CRM is a system with four connected parts, not a quarterly project. The matching keys, merge classes, survivorship rules and enforcement we had to write down before deduplication could run as code.
articles.title: CRM Hygiene: The Rules We Had to Write Down to Turn It Into Code

articles.summary: Agents now write most changes to a revenue engine, and a GTM stack configured by clicking has no place to review them. Why the migration to git is due now, what moves first, what stays in the UI, and how teams have done it in under a day.
articles.title: Why GTM Teams Need to Migrate Their Stack to Git

articles.summary: The most expensive leak in outbound is a yes nobody answers. How an agent can research, classify and draft the reply to every response across email and LinkedIn, and why the human approval step is the part to keep until the classifier earns trust.
articles.title: Answering Positive Replies in Minutes, Not Hours

articles.summary: The layer between the warehouse, the CRM and the tools reps work in. What middleware has to do that a sync does not (identity resolution, a schema contract, conflict rules, idempotency, back-pressure, a trace), and how to tell whether you need it or just need one more pipeline.
articles.title: Revenue Data Middleware for GTM Operations

articles.summary: The same qualification rule ends up written in the CRM, the marketing tool, a warehouse model and a rep's saved view, and the four disagree. Why logic scatters across platforms, what belongs in each tool, and how to define a rule once and let every system execute it.
articles.title: Cross-Platform Revenue Logic: Where GTM Rules Should Live

articles.summary: Salesforce assignment rules and HubSpot workflows route on the fields the CRM holds. What to do when the rule needs rep capacity, an account match, product usage or a score computed elsewhere: the three classes of alternative, and what capacity-aware routing looks like declared as code.
articles.title: Modern Alternatives to CRM-Native Lead Routing and Assignment

articles.summary: Agentic GTM infrastructure is what a self-driving GTM engine runs on: AI agents defined and deployed as code, orchestration workflows callable from the UI, the CLI, the API and agents, and one unified data model behind lead routing and scoring.
articles.title: Building a Self-Driving GTM Engine with Agentic Infrastructure

articles.summary: Pipeline targets tell you the number missed. They do not tell you which stage leaked. How to instrument pipeline generation as a system with inputs, yield and latency per stage, what to measure at each seam, and where agents belong once the instrument exists.
articles.title: Revenue Pipeline Engineering: Treating Pipeline as a System

articles.summary: A weekly job that reads pipeline data, finds the accounts your scoring model is wrongly suppressing, and opens a pull request with the fix and its blast radius. How Plain built it, and how to build your own.
articles.title: Let an Agent Propose Changes to Your Scoring Model

articles.summary: Agents write the code now. What decides whether a GTM system lasts is the data underneath it: durable tables, keys that mean one thing, identity resolution, and one writer per fact. The four ideas to learn first, and the mistakes each one prevents.
articles.title: Data Architecture for GTM Engineers: What to Learn First

articles.summary: Qualification is not a tool, it is a pipeline that crosses four systems: capture, identity resolution, enrichment, decision, write-back and follow-up. Where it breaks at each seam, what to ask of a platform, and how to build the rubric as versioned code.
articles.title: How to Qualify a List of Leads Against Your ICP

articles.summary: Who should GTM Engineering report to? Data from 1,784 job offers shows how the right reporting line changes from startup to enterprise.
articles.title: Who Should GTM Engineering Report To? 2026 Data

articles.summary: A signal that is three months too old sends a rep to the wrong account with the wrong reason. How to give every signal an expiry window and a weight, why the simplest version is a WHERE clause, and why verification comes before any of it.
articles.title: How Long Is a Buying Signal Worth? Time Decay, Weights, and Verification

articles.summary: A target account list is correct on the day it is built and decays from then on. What it takes to run the market as a recomputed ranking instead: the inputs that move, the scoring function, the activation loop, and what to instrument so the order can be defended.
articles.title: Turning a TAM Into Prioritized Pipeline, Continuously

articles.summary: A hard ICP cutoff, set once and revisited quarterly, silently suppresses accounts that are showing real buying intent. How it happens, the weekly query that finds them, and how to change the rule without throwing the ICP away.
articles.title: Your ICP Filter Is Hiding Your Hottest Accounts

articles.summary: More startups now run go-to-market from a git repository and a database, and add a CRM later. When that works, what a CRM actually gives you that a repo does not, and the signs it is time to buy one.
articles.title: Do Early-Stage Startups Still Need a CRM?

articles.summary: When a GTM engineering team should build revenue infrastructure in-house and when to buy a platform: what the second year of a custom stack costs, where the line sits layer by layer, and what one system can honestly replace.
articles.title: Build vs Buy: Scaling Your GTM Engineering Stack in 2026

articles.summary: Signals live in six tools, the account list is a three-week-old spreadsheet, and reps prospect on gut. The fix is not another tab in the CRM: it is an activity layer with its rules in git, its data in one place, and the reason for every account on screen.
articles.title: The Missing Layer Between Your CRM and Your Reps
